name: Tarcondimotid Kingdom
alt: Client kingdom of Anazarbus and Castabala

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: Upper Cilicia: 'Anazarbus and Castabala, plus the regions of Bryclice, Characene, and Lacanitis, and ... strongholds on Mount Amanus' (the 66-63 BC holdings on the page)

rulers.name: Tarcondimotus I
rulers.title: toparch of Upper Cilicia from c. 70 BC; king from c. 38 BC

ledger.x: 66 BC or after: Pompey confirms Tarcondimotus as toparch of Upper Cilicia.
66 BC or after: Upper Cilicia is a Roman client under Pompey's settlement.

c. 38 BC: Mark Antony grants Tarcondimotus the royal title. 'Antony granted him the royal title c.38 BC' in recognition of his loyalty against the Parthian invasion of 40 BC; Pompey 'did not recognize him as king'. The state and its land continue; the toparchy becomes a kingdom. The year is the…
31 BC: Tarcondimotus I dies at Actium and the royal title lapses.
27 BC: the client relation passes from the Republic to the Empire.
27 BC: Upper Cilicia is a client of the new Roman Empire.
20 BC: Augustus restores the royal title.
AD 17: the last Tarcondimotid king dies and Rome annexes Upper Cilicia.

wars.name: Battle of Actium (Tarcondimotus I on Antony's side)
wars.outcome: Tarcondimotus I 'died fighting on Antony's behalf at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC'; Octavian stripped his son of the royal title within the year.

certainty.note: Towns and mountain names, no frontier.
